clue.text: Funny gag rated without a sign of being made worse

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the next piece
funny can mean odd or peculiar, so the letters that follow are put into an odd order

parts.note: the two words taken as letters to rearrange
taken as written
the V-sign, a rude hand gesture

explanation.surface: A comedian's gag, rated poorly with no sign of approval, made things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-sign is a rude British hand gesture; here sign is just the letter V.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggravate a problem is to intensify it, so aggravated is a synonym of made worse.

clue.text: Break in new rafter containing elements copper

indicators.note: containing means the timber word holds the element symbol inside it
new suggests a fresh version, so the combined letters are made over into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol of the element copper

explanation.surface: A builder spots a break in a new roof beam reinforced with copper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a crack or break, especially in a bone or hard material.

clue.text: Lay stress on part of bargain sister made

indicators.note: part of says the letters sit inside a longer run of the clue's words

parts.note: the run spans the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: A sister drives a hard bargain at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across bargaIN SISTer.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly or emphasise a point, which is laying stress on it.

clue.text: Massive squeeze at one point

parts.note: a hug is an affectionate squeeze
east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A huge squeeze at one stage of the game, perhaps a tight moment in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge and massive are synonyms, both describing something of enormous size.

clue.text: Cuts across site compound

indicators.note: to compound is to mix things together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply all ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A path cuts across a building compound on site.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuts looks like a verb about paths; it is the definition, in the sense of snubbing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore them deliberately, and to ostracise is to exclude them socially.

clue.text: Vanish when question framed in triumph

indicators.note: something framed is surrounded, so the first word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A contestant disappears in glory when the final question is put to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph over an enemy is to defeat them, which is what vanquish means; triumph is used as a verb.

clue.text: They say it's cold at the border

indicators.note: they say points to what people speak, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: freeze, extreme cold, has the same sound

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that the weather is bitter at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: Border looks like a national frontier, but here it is a decorative band along a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a horizontal decorative band running along a wall, an ornamental border.

clue.text: Leading characters in comedy at seaside theatre

definitions.text: Leading characters in comedy at seaside theatre

indicators.note: leading characters are the ones at the front of each word, so we take the initials

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: The stars of a summer comedy show at a seaside theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and leading characters also tells you to take initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast is the set of actors playing the characters in a show.

clue.text: Measuring arrangement of flowers

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A florist measures out stems for a flower arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrangement of flowers reads as a bouquet; arrangement is the signal and flowers alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraniums are common garden and pot plants grown for their bright blooms.

clue.text: Article on new rota for a major vessel

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: new hints at a revised version, so the duty list is reordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A newsletter article about a new duty roster on a large ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a ship, but here it is a blood vessel. A rota is a schedule of turns of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery of the body, the largest blood vessel.

clue.text: Get daughter to leave cunning deceiver

indicators.note: cunning suggests craftiness or artful working, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to leave says one letter departs from the word it was in

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent urges their daughter to walk out on a crafty liar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cunning looks like an adjective for the deceiver, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something, such as a letter or gift, is to receive it; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Ask about hunt

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a quest is a search or hunt

explanation.walkthrough: About looks like part of the phrase ask about; it gives RE, and Ask stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To request is to ask for something politely or formally.

clue.text: Museum using local themes, primarily in spring

parts.note: the V&A, the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of those words count

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A museum's spring exhibition built around local themes.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum, London's museum of art and design. Spring looks like the season but is the verb to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to leap over something, and spring is a synonym for jump or leap.

clue.text: Colouring abnormal in cochlea

indicators.note: abnormal means not in the usual form, so these letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A doctor notes an unusual discolouration inside the ear's cochlea.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a link word but its letters are needed; the cochlea is the spiral part of the inner ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a red dye made from crushed insects and used as food colouring.

clue.text: Horrible laceration that harks back to the beginning

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled or messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A nasty cut that takes someone back to the start of their trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase standing loosely for an adjective: something that harks back to the beginning is concerned with creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Creational relates to creation, the very beginning of the world, so it looks back to the origin.

clue.text: In place of one renting to person with military rank

parts.note: in lieu of means in place of
a tenant rents a property

explanation.surface: A lodger who rents a room to a soldier instead of someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieu, from French, survives in English mainly in the phrase in lieu of.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a commissioned officer rank in the army or navy.

clue.text: Those in charge found wheat better — shop around!

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about and turned round, so the preceding words are set in a new order

parts.note: all three words supply the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The bosses discovered better grain by shopping around for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Shop around reads as a familiar phrase urging comparison of prices, but shop is fodder and around alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the people holding authority, the establishment that makes decisions.

clue.text: Decorate vase, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to adorn
second meaning: a noun, a decorative object

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to decorate a vase; the two halves are separate meanings, one verb and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornament as a verb means to adorn, and as a noun names a decorative object such as a vase.

clue.text: Raise the volume or stop it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: increase the sound on a radio or stereo
second meaning: a British slang exclamation telling someone to quit

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent shouts at a teenager playing loud music: louder, or quit!
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the phrase is also a dated exclamation meaning stop that or give over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to increase volume, and as slang it is an order to cease doing something.

clue.text: Donates without mercenary incentive initially and rules the roost

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word wraps around the selected letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so we keep only the first letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A boss gives money freely, with no selfish motive, and is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like lacking; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule the roost is an idiom for being in control, which is to dominate.

clue.text: Mix without stirring tar to make the mould

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word wraps around the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: stirring moves contents around, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Instructions for blending tar without stirring before casting a mould.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix and stirring both look like the recipe's verbs; Mix gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a mould in which something is cast or shaped, such as type in printing.

clue.text: Original tree, by the way

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An old tree, and by the way, it is the original one.
explanation.walkthrough: By the way reads as an aside; by joins, and the way gives the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of something is the original one, the earliest from which others follow.

clue.text: Crime: offender unknown

parts.note: a felon is someone who has committed a serious crime
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A crime has been committed and the culprit has not been identified.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious crime, more grave than a misdemeanour in legal terms.

clue.text: Faster ascension time

parts.note: ascension is a going up
tempo is musical time, the speed of a piece

explanation.surface: A quicker climb, measured against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptempo describes music played at a quick pace, so it is faster than the norm.

clue.text: Reverse effects partially at sundown

indicators.note: partially means only a part of the following word is used, the letters inside it

parts.note: the letters sit inside the word, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: Something reverses its effects in part at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse looks like a turnaround signal, but the letters read forwards inside sUNDOwn; Reverse belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to cancel out or reverse what has been done.

clue.text: One on account first for a huge sum

indicators.note: first places the account word ahead of the earlier-mentioned pieces

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Putting someone on the account first costs a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces out of order; first moves the account word to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A billion is a thousand million, an enormous number.

clue.text: Reserve of former student going back on agreement

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the abbreviation is read right to left

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: An alumnus backs out of a deal held in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an old boy is a former pupil of a school, abbreviated OB.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to reserve it in advance.

clue.text: Condescend to hear a person from Scandinavia

indicators.note: to hear points to listening, so the answer matches the sound of the next words

parts.note: a Dane comes from Denmark

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to listen to a visitor from Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to do something one considers beneath one's dignity, so condescend is a synonym.

clue.text: One low act experiencing a fall

parts.note: a means one
feeling low is feeling down
a turn is a performance or act on stage

explanation.surface: A performer in a sad act tumbles over on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a short act in a variety show.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a decline, such as in the economy, so it amounts to a fall.
